messages:
Asha (ML Eng): Pushed a fresh onboard run for lyra-v2 (q5) on staging. Quick heads-up: mixed-script detok glitches in two places: Japanese kana+kanji slices sometimes reorder brackets, and Arabic RTL contexts show punctuation mirror flips on long replies. Anyone free to help triage?
Ren (NLP Evals): Can you paste minimal repro examples and the eval job id? Ill add locale-focused diffs.
Asha (ML Eng): run id: lyra-v2-eval-2026-03-22-09. Repro (minimized): "Input: 
JP sample: 日本[カタ] -> Detok: 日本]カタ[ (brackets swapped)
AR sample: المثال (note: [check]) -> Detok long: المثال )note: ]check[
Asha (ML Eng): These repros are from the q5 quantized variant; fp16 baseline didn't show them.
Lina (Quant): Which q5 profile? per-channel symmetric or per-tensor? Different scale strategies can nudge subtoken logits and change boundaries.
Asha (ML Eng): q5 symmetric per-channel, same bucket as our standard onboard.
Diego (Serving): My guess: detok reordering combined with KV cache prefix merging. If prefix cache slices the output into segments with stale position metadata, a subsequent ICU bidi pass could mis-handle embedded LTR spans.
Ibrahim (Localization): Arabic flipping on long outputs sounds like a bidi reflow issue. Could be we call Unicode bidi twice or in the wrong order relative to punctuation normalization.
Ren (NLP Evals): I'll run a deterministic suite: short/medium/long contexts for zh/ja/ko/ar with prefix-cache on/off and with/without post-detok ICU bidi call. Will collect BLEU/chrF and a micro-detok diff that flags paired-punct flips.
ci-bot: scheduled job lyra-v2-eval-2026-03-22-09 started (jobs: 12 locales).
Lina (Quant): Also check embedding table folding and any recent kernel patches. Our int8-per-channel run on aurora had a tiny token-shift before, which showed only in detok-sensitive locales.
Asha (ML Eng): Plan: A) q5 + prefix-cache-on (current), B) q5 + prefix-cache-off, C) fallback fp16 detok for rtl locales, D) try int8-per-channel variant. Running A/B/C now, D queued.
Diego (Serving): I will add a detok unit runner that takes token ids + byte offsets + prefix-metadata and prints reordering operations. If we can reproduce offline we can add a unit test.
Ren (NLP Evals): Adding a small script to the eval pipeline that compares canonicalized detok outputs (NFKC + unified bidi) and emits a compact "pair-flip" diff; will attach to CI run artifacts.
Lina (Quant): If you run int8 variant, be sure to tag the run with quant checksum and compiler kext version. We had a silent change after kext 2.14.1.
Asha (ML Eng): Noted; tag included. Quick intermediate result: with prefix-cache disabled, JP bracket swap rate drops from 0.7% -> 0.02% on 5k sample subset. Arabic mirror still reproducible at ~1.2% for long contexts.
Ibrahim (Localization): For Arabic, can you share an example where the mirror happens only after 120 tokens? Different shaping/cursor placement at >column wrap could trigger a second bidi pass.
Asha (ML Eng): Example attached in the run artifact (short gist): https://internal.gists/asha/lyra-rtl-repro. That one flips after the model emits an embedded English clause and then continues for 80+ tokens.
Diego (Serving): I reproduced the Arabic mirror locally by running detok with the same position metadata sequence; disabling the final ICU bidi call yields correct punctuation orientation but might break desired locale shaping. We need to preserve shaping while avoiding double-reorder.
Ren (NLP Evals): Eval job completed (partial): ja->en BLEU delta -0.4 (q5 vs fp16), ko->en -0.3, ar->en -1.4. Attached detok-diff.tsv with flagged pair-flips per sample.
Lina (Quant): Running int8-per-channel now; will post results soon. If int8 fixes it, we're back to quant-induced token shuffling hypothesis.
Asha (ML Eng): If int8 also shows the issue, probably detok logic; Diego, can we add a cheap guard: for rtl locales, run bidi in a mode tolerant to prefixed position offsets?
Diego (Serving): Yes we can add a permissive ICU flag or fallback to fp16 detok for rtl locales as short-term mitigation. I'll prototype both and bench.
Ibrahim (Localization): Short-term mitigation approved by localization: fallback to fp16 detok on ar/he while triage continues. That preserves customer-facing stability.
ci-bot: job lyra-v2-eval-2026-03-22-09:int8 finished. int8-per-channel results: ja->en BLEU delta -0.35, ko->en -0.28, ar->en -0.6 (improved vs q5 but not fully baseline). Detok pair-flips reduced to 0.3% for ar. Full artifacts: https://ci/internal/evals/lyra-v2/2026-03-22-09/int8
Ren (NLP Evals): Interesting: int8 reduces Arabic flips but doesn't eliminate them. That points to both quant nudging token boundaries and a detok bidi sensitivity.
Lina (Quant): I'll diff token-id sequences between fp16 and q5/int8 for flagged samples to see if token boundary shifts correlate.
Asha (ML Eng): Action items: 1) Diego add permissive bidi flag + fp16-detok fallback (short-term), 2) Lina produce token-id diffs for flagged samples, 3) Ren attach per-sample detok diffs and pair-flip list, 4) Ibrahim confirm localization integration tests pass with fp16 fallback. I'll update this thread with mitigation timeline.
Diego (Serving): Added permissive-bidi prototype to staging; perf impact negligible. Will roll to canary after CI.
Lina (Quant): Token-id diffs uploaded: many arabic flagged samples show a 1-token shift around LTR embedded clauses in q5 vs fp16; int8 reduces but doesn't fully remove. Patch note in artifact.
Ren (NLP Evals): Localization regression tests pass with fp16 detok fallback on canary.
Asha (ML Eng): Good. We'll ship fp16 detok fallback for rtl locales and continue triage on tokenization + quant cross-talk. Thanks everyone. If new findings, drop here."
